title: In re Palmer Center Foreclosure — Wells Fargo Tower & FirstBank Building (Colorado Springs Public Trustee Foreclosure)
jurisdiction: El Paso County Public Trustee, Colorado (non-judicial foreclosure)
amount: ~$59M unpaid principal balance on an original $74M loan
summary: El Paso County Public Trustee's Office records show foreclosure notices filed against RPalmer LLC, Overland Palmer LLC, and Palmer Center Owner LLC — Delaware entities controlled by California-based real estate investment and management companies — over a loan with an unpaid principal balance of roughly $59 million against an original $74 million facility. The filings cover downtown Colorado Springs' two tallest buildings, the Wells Fargo Tower and FirstBank Building at the Palmer Center complex, plus several ancillary business-suite properties reachable through either tower.
significance: A marquee, long-tenured downtown office complex defaulting on debt service — rather than a commodity suburban asset — signals that post-pandemic office distress has moved beyond the most obviously troubled properties. Owners, lenders, and asset managers with loans maturing in secondary downtown markets should treat trophy status and blue-chip anchor tenancies as no longer sufficient on their own to guarantee refinancing in the current rate environment.
